title: Indian Creator Swati Tries Japan's Viral 10-Layer Matcha Mont Blanc, Rates It 8 Out of 10
excerpt: At Chacha Futatsume in Tokyo, what looks like a giant ice cream cone hides lemon marmalade, red bean paste, cake and mascarpone — and costs Rs 840.
body:
• Indian content creator Swati tried the viral Matcha Mont Blanc at Chacha Futatsume in Tokyo and called it a "beautiful deception" — it looks like a giant cone of ice cream but is not ice cream.
  • Inside are 10 layers; the combination that surprised her most was lemon marmalade with red bean paste, alongside cream, cake, matcha syrup and mascarpone.
  • She rated the dessert 8 out of 10 and noted the price in her video: Rs 840 for one dessert.
  • According to the shop's description carried in the reports, the dessert has eight components, including green tea chestnut, mashed bean paste, sponge cake, agar jelly and a gold leaf on top.

It looks like a giant cone of soft-serve ice cream. It is not. That is the warning Indian content creator Swati gave viewers after trying Japan's viral Matcha Mont Blanc during a visit to Tokyo, NDTV Food's report, carried by Dainik News Live

"Don't be fooled by this viral dessert in Japan because you'll dig in thinking it's ice cream until it's not. You'll either love it or hate it. There is no in-between."

— Swati, content creator, in her video

Swati visited Chacha Futatsume in Tokyo to try its famous Matcha Mont Blanc, calling the dessert a "beautiful deception" in her account of the tasting.

Ten Layers, None of Them Expected

The first bite, she said, hit her with strong matcha. Then the layers kept changing. "The first bite hit me with strong matcha… but as we kept going deeper, it started making sense. There was lemon marmalade with red bean paste, cream, cake… and a bunch of flavours we honestly weren't expecting to find inside something that looked this simple," she wrote alongside the video.

The layer that shocked her most was the lemon marmalade with red bean paste. According to the dessert shop's description cited in the reports, the 10-layered dessert has eight components: green tea chestnut, mashed bean paste, lemon marmalade, green tea syrup, sponge cake, agar jelly, mascarpone cream and a gold leaf on top. Earlier coverage by Curly Tales of the same dessert at Chacha Futatsume in Asakusa, Tokyo, lists the same components and describes the shop as a Japanese tea cafe serving desserts made with organic Japanese tea.

The Making Is Half the Show

Part of the appeal is watching it being built. "Watching them pipe those matcha strands layer by layer until this crazy-looking thing is sitting on the cone was half the fun. And then you realise there are 10 layers inside this thing," Swati wrote. The piped green strands are what give the Mont Blanc its noodle-like, soft-serve appearance — and what sets up the surprise when a spoon goes in and finds cake, jelly and bean paste instead.

The Verdict — and the Price

Her final score was clear: "Overall an eight on ten for this Matcha Mont Blanc." The price was the caveat. "It was an 8/10 for us, but Rs 840 for a dessert is definitely not cheap," she wrote. Curly Tales, in its earlier report, put the price at ¥1,200, around Rs 730 at the time — a reminder that the viral cone sits firmly in treat territory, not everyday snack territory.

For Indian travellers heading to Tokyo, the practical lesson from Swati's video is about expectations, not avoidance: order it for the layers and the theatre of the piping, expect strong matcha first and tart marmalade and red bean further down, and do not expect ice cream. As she put it, you will either love it or hate it — there is no in-between.
